sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered a clean, renewable source of energy?
What causes the continuous cycle of seasons on Earth?
options: A) The rotation of the Earth on its axis
B) The revolution of the Earth around the Sun
C) The changing phases of the Moon
D) The movement of ocean tides
questions.answer: B) The revolution of the Earth around the Sun

questions.question_text: Which natural raw material is primarily used to make cotton clothes?
options: C) Cotton bolls from a plant
questions.answer: C) Cotton bolls from a plant

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a famous unique monument in India built entirely of white marble?
What does the 'Reduce, Reuse, Recycle' rule help us achieve?
options: B) Protect and conserve the environment
C) Waste more energy at home
questions.answer: B) Protect and conserve the environment

questions.question_text: Who operates the loom to turn yarn into large sheets of fabric?
Which type of energy powers most of our modern devices like televisions, refrigerators, and computers?
What usually happens to deciduous trees during the autumn season?
options: A) They grow new, bright flowers
B) They are covered in heavy snow
C) Their leaves change color and fall off
D) They grow fruit very rapidly
questions.answer: C) Their leaves change color and fall off

questions.question_text: Why is the Earth often referred to as a 'shared home'?
options: A) It belongs exclusively to humans
B) It is shared by humans, plants, and animals
C) Only wild animals are allowed to live here
D) It is owned by one single country
questions.answer: B) It is shared by humans, plants, and animals

questions.question_text: Which historical site is famous for its ancient rock-cut caves and stunning paintings in Maharashtra?
Why is it important to switch from using fossil fuels to solar and wind energy? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Fossil fuels cause heavy pollution and will eventually run out. Solar and wind energy are clean, renewable, and help protect the environment from harmful greenhouse gases.

questions.question_text: Briefly describe the role of a weaver in making clothes. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A weaver uses a machine called a loom to tightly interlace long threads of yarn together, creating large sheets of fabric that are later cut and stitched.

questions.question_text: How does the tilt of the Earth affect our seasons? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Earth's tilt causes different parts to receive varying amounts of direct sunlight during its orbit. The part tilted toward the Sun experiences summer, while the other experiences winter.

questions.question_text: What is meant by an 'ecosystem' in nature? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: An ecosystem is a natural community where living things like plants, animals, and humans interact with each other and their non-living environment, such as soil, water, and air.

questions.question_text: Why should we protect and preserve historical monuments and unique places? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Historical monuments are unique treasures that teach us about our rich cultural heritage, ancient architecture, and the fascinating lives of people who lived centuries ago.

questions.question_text: Imagine you visit a large textile mill. Describe the process of transforming plain yarn into beautiful, finished clothes. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Inside the noisy mill, machines quickly weave raw yarn into long sheets of fabric. The fabric is then washed, dyed into bright colors, and printed with beautiful patterns. Finally, skilled tailors cut the cloth and stitch it together to make fashionable garments.

questions.question_text: Imagine experiencing the transition from a hot summer to the monsoon season. Describe the changes in the sky and the environment. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The blazing hot sun is suddenly hidden by thick, dark grey clouds rolling across the sky. Cool breezes replace the hot air, and soon, heavy raindrops begin to fall, turning the dry, dusty earth into a lush, vibrant green landscape smelling of fresh soil.

questions.question_text: Explain how students can adopt energy-efficient habits at home and school to reduce their reliance on fossil fuels. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Students can save energy by always turning off lights, fans, and computers when leaving a room. They can maximize natural sunlight by opening curtains during the day, use bicycles or walk for short distances, and remind adults to use energy-efficient appliances, which collectively reduces the burning of fossil fuels.

questions.question_text: Discuss the concept of 'Earth Our Shared Home' and suggest actionable steps we can take to protect local wildlife and green spaces. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The Earth belongs equally to humans, plants, and animals, meaning we must share its resources responsibly. We can protect local wildlife by not littering in parks, planting native flowers to feed bees and butterflies, building bird feeders, and organizing neighborhood clean-up drives to keep natural habitats safe and beautiful.
